articles.title: BRICS issues New Delhi Declaration, as UAE and Iran back down from tough positions - The Hindu
articles.description: The BRICS bloc adopted the 'New Delhi Declaration' during its latest summit, emphasizing resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainability. India played a pivotal diplomatic role in bridging differences between newly added members, Iran and the United Arab Emirates (UAE), to achieve full consensus. The declaration focuses on multilateral reform, economic integration, counter-terrorism, and strengthening regional stability. For competitive exams, note the expansion of BRICS (originally Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa) to include new members like the UAE, Iran, Egypt, and Ethiopia.

articles.title: India’s central bank tells Tata Sons to take conglomerate public - Financial Times
articles.description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) rejected Tata Sons' application to surrender its Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) license, mandating its public listing. Under RBI's Scale Based Regulation (SBR) framework introduced in 2021, Tata Sons is classified as an 'Upper Layer' NBFC (NBFC-UL) due to its systemic importance. NBFC-UL entities are subject to enhanced regulatory oversight and must mandatorily list on stock exchanges within three years of identification to ensure greater transparency, corporate governance, and financial stability in India's shadow banking sector.

articles.title: India rules out Brics currency proposal, backs local currency trade settlements - The Times of India
articles.description: India has officially ruled out proposals for a common BRICS currency, advocating instead for national currency trade settlements to facilitate international commerce. While supporting de-dollarisation and global financial reforms, India emphasizes strengthening local currency cross-border payment systems (like UPI-based linkages and Special Vostro Rupee Accounts). This approach aims to reduce transaction costs and currency volatility without creating a rigid monetary union. Additionally, the stance highlights India's push for reforming voting quotas and governance structures in international financial institutions like the IMF and World Bank.

articles.title: DFCs: The backbone of India’s logistics push
articles.description: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC) has become fully operational, establishing a 2,843-km dedicated rail network with the Eastern DFC (EDFC) to transform national logistics. Executed by the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) under the Ministry of Railways, DFCs are designed to segregate freight movement from passenger traffic. This infrastructure milestone supports the National Logistics Policy, aiming to reduce India's logistics costs from 13–14% of GDP to single digits, enhance freight train speeds, and boost industrial corridors.

articles.title: India and EU close to sealing trade deal, await nod from top Council in Brussels - The Indian Express
articles.description: India and the European Union (EU) are nearing finalization of a landmark Free Trade Agreement (FTA), pending approval from the European Council in Brussels. Negotiations encompass three main pillars: trade in goods and services, investment protection, and Geographical Indications (GIs). The EU remains one of India's largest trade partners and investors. Key discussion areas include lowering tariffs on automobiles and spirits, market access, regulatory alignment, and addressing EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) to boost bilateral trade resilience.

articles.title: Asia Cup: Indian women's cricket team refuses to accept trophy from ACC head Mohsin Naqvi
articles.description: The Indian women’s cricket team, led by Captain Harmanpreet Kaur, secured their record-extending eighth Women's Asia Cup title by defeating Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final. The Asian Cricket Council (ACC), established in 1983 to promote and develop cricket across Asia, organizes the tournament. The event highlights India's dominance in regional women's cricket. For competitive exams, key facts include India's 8th title win, ACC headquarters in Dubai, UAE, and the role of ACC under the International Cricket Council (ICC) framework.

articles.title: S-400 destroyed Pakistani aircraft at 314 km during Operation Sindoor: Defence Ministry report - thehindu.com
articles.description: According to a Ministry of Defence report, India's S-400 air defense system successfully engaged and destroyed a target at a range of 314 km during Operation Sindoor. The S-400 Triumf is a mobile, surface-to-air missile (SAM) system developed by Russia's Almaz-Antey, capable of intercepting aircraft, drones, and ballistic missiles up to 400 km. Acquired under an intergovernmental agreement signed between India and Russia in 2018, the system significantly enhances the Indian Air Force’s (IAF) long-range air defense capabilities and integrated air command network.

articles.title: UCC in all 21 NDA-ruled States by 2029: Amit Shah - thehindu.com
articles.description: Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) across all 21 NDA-ruled states by 2029. UCC is enshrined under Article 44 of Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy) of the Indian Constitution, which mandates the state to secure a uniform set of civil laws governing marriage, divorce, inheritance, and adoption for all citizens regardless of religion. Uttarakhand recently became the first post-independence Indian state to pass a UCC bill, setting a legal precedent for state-level implementations.

articles.title: India to get 1.64 million-tonne EU steel quota; 6.95 lakh tonnes under FTA - Moneycontrol.com
articles.description: Under ongoing negotiations for the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA), India has secured a 1.64 million-tonne annual steel quota, including 6.95 lakh tonnes under preferential FTA terms. The proposed agreement also allows the import of 1,000,000 cars from the EU at reduced tariff rates during its initial year. Overseen by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the trade deal aims to enhance bilateral commerce, ease tariff barriers, and expand Indian steel exports, while addressing European Union trade safeguard measures and carbon import regulations.

articles.title: Brics opposes unilateral trade steps like EU carbon border tax - The Times of India
articles.description: The BRICS bloc voiced strong opposition to unilateral trade restrictions, specifically targeting the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). BRICS members argued that such carbon border taxes violate World Trade Organization (WTO) norms and the principle of Common But Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) under the UNFCCC. Instead, the grouping advocated for voluntary carbon market cooperation and climate finance for developing nations. The development highlights rising trade tensions over green protectionism and its impact on emerging economies' industrial exports, including Indian steel and aluminum.

articles.title: Govt. bars bank charges on payments up to ₹2,000 via UPI, RuPay-powered debit cards
articles.description: The Union Government has prohibited banks from levying charges or Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on transactions up to ₹2,000 executed via Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and RuPay debit cards. Issued under amendments to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, this decision aims to boost digital payments penetration across small merchants. Developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) in 2016, UPI operates under RBI guidelines. This zero-MDR mandate supports financial inclusion while strengthening digital financial infrastructure.

articles.title: India approves expedited export of electricity to flood-hit Nepal
articles.description: The Union Ministry of Power approved the expedited export of electricity to flood-hit Nepal to meet its urgent energy demands. Managed under Cross-Border Electricity Trade (CBET) guidelines, the initiative highlights India’s Neighborhood First policy and bilateral energy cooperation. Central Electricity Authority (CEA) acts as the designated authority for cross-border power trade approvals. India and Nepal share sub-regional energy integration mechanisms, including power purchase agreements and joint hydro-project initiatives like the Arun-III power project, reinforcing regional power grid connectivity.

articles.title: Pakistan names Jaish chief Masood Azhar among most wanted terrorists, hikes bounty to PKR 70 lakh ahead of FATF review | World News - Hindustan Times
articles.description: Pakistan announced a bounty of PKR 70 lakh for Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) chief Masood Azhar ahead of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) plenary review. Azhar was designated a global terrorist by the UN Security Council’s 1267 Sanctions Committee in May 2019. FATF, established in 1989 by G7 countries and headquartered in Paris, monitors global money laundering and terror financing. Countries non-compliant with FATF anti-money laundering standards face placement on the Grey or Black Lists, incurring severe international financial restrictions.

articles.title: India, Canada begin next round of talks on proposed trade pact: Official
articles.description: India and Canada initiated negotiations for an Early Progress Trade Agreement (EPTA) as a step toward a full Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA). Overseen by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the trade pact aims to expand bilateral trade to $50 billion by 2030. Key focus areas include pharmaceuticals, clean energy, agriculture, critical minerals, and services. Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) like CEPA lower tariff barriers, boost bilateral investments, and facilitate trade integration between negotiating partner nations.

articles.title: WPI inflation rises to 9.92% in August on rising prices of food, fuel, manufactured items
articles.description: India's Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation rose to 9.92% in August, driven by surges in food, fuel, and manufactured items, which hit a series high of 8.37%. WPI measures wholesale price changes and is published monthly by the Office of the Economic Adviser, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, with 2011-12 as its base year. The index comprises Primary Articles (22.62%), Fuel and Power (13.15%), and Manufactured Products (64.23%). Unlike CPI, WPI excludes service sector inflation.

articles.title: Decoding India’s GDP base revision
articles.description: India's Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) periodically revises the base year for Gross Domestic Product (GDP) calculations to better reflect structural shifts in the economy. A major driver for upcoming revisions is the enhanced statistical coverage and improved measurement of the unorganized and unincorporated services sector. Updating base years aligns GDP estimates with international System of National Accounts (SNA) standards, capturing updated consumption patterns and new economic activities for precise macroeconomic policy formulation by the government and the RBI.

articles.title: Six States, UT sign Kishau multipurpose project agreement; CM Sukhu hails ‘major victory’ for Himachal
articles.description: Six beneficiary states/UTs—including Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Haryana, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan—have signed an agreement for the Kishau Multipurpose Project. Located on the Tons River, a major tributary of the Yamuna River along the Uttarakhand-Himachal Pradesh border, this 660 MW hydro-electric project aims to generate power and provide irrigation and drinking water. Classified as a Project of National Importance, the central government funds 90% of the water component, enhancing inter-state water sharing, regional power grid supply, and flood moderation capabilities.

articles.title: August retail inflation raises chances of RBI rate hike in October, say economists
articles.description: India's retail inflation, measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI) released by the National Statistical Office (NSO), rose to a 20-month high of 4.8% in August, driven primarily by surging food prices. Under the Monetary Policy Framework, the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) targets headline CPI inflation at 4% with a tolerance band of 2% to 6%. Rising inflationary pressures restrict the central bank's room for monetary easing and increase the likelihood of benchmark repo rate hikes to anchor inflation expectations.

articles.title: Expect EU to sign FTA and India-Canada negotiations to be completed by year-end, govt says
articles.description: The Union Ministry of Commerce and Industry announced significant progress in India's bilateral trade negotiations, expecting the completion of negotiations with Canada and major strides on the India-EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA). Additionally, trade talks with the U.S. focus on resolving bilateral tariff issues and finalizing a long-delayed interim trade agreement. FTAs aim to reduce tariff barriers, expand market access for Indian goods and services, streamline supply chains, and boost foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows across crucial industrial and service sectors.

articles.title: India’s 26% goods exports surge lowers August 2026 trade deficit
articles.description: According to the Department of Commerce, India's merchandise exports witnessed a robust 26% growth, outpacing import growth in both percentage and absolute terms to significantly narrow the trade deficit. The surge was driven by high demand in key engineering, petroleum, chemical, and electronics sectors. The trade deficit—the difference between the monetary value of merchandise imports and exports—directly influences the Current Account Deficit (CAD). Strong foreign trade metrics help bolster foreign exchange reserves and strengthen the Indian Rupee against macroeconomic volatility.

articles.title: Hog in the limelight: On Assam’s pygmy hog programme
articles.description: The Pygmy Hog (Porcula salvania), the world's smallest and rarest wild pig, is an indicator species for tall alluvial grassland ecosystems. Endemic to Assam, its population severely declined due to habitat loss. The Pygmy Hog Conservation Programme (PHCP)—a collaboration involving the Assam Forest Department, Durrell Wildlife Conservation Trust, and MoEFCC—has successfully reintroduced captive-bred individuals into Manas National Park, Orang National Park, and Barnadi Wildlife Sanctuary. Listed as Endangered under the IUCN Red List and protected under Schedule I of India's Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, its survival relies heavily on grassland management.

articles.title: India rejects Pakistan-China Boundary Joint Commission ‘which is without any legal basis’ - The Hindu
articles.description: India’s Ministry of External Affairs rejected the establishment of a "Boundary Joint Commission" between Pakistan and China, declaring it legally void. India asserts that the entire Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh are integral parts of India. Under the illegal 1963 Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement, Pakistan unlawfully ceded over 5,000 sq km of Indian territory in Shaksgam Valley (PoK) to China. New Delhi reiterated that neither Islamabad nor Beijing has locus standi to alter the status of occupied Indian territories or establish border commissions without legal standing.

articles.title: After 12 years, Centre hikes EPFO wage ceiling to ₹25,000 a month
articles.description: The Union Ministry of Labour and Employment announced an increase in the monthly wage ceiling under the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000, marking the first hike since 2014. Under the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, mandatory coverage applies to firms with 20 or more workers. The revision raises the maximum monthly contribution to the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) to ₹2,082.50. This move aims to expand formal social security, expectedly adding 51 lakh to 1 crore new subscribers into the institutional pension framework.

articles.title: India renegotiates treaties with Mauritius, Singapore, Cyprus to restore right to tax capital gains at so - The Times of India
articles.description: India has renegotiated Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAA) with key investment corridors including Mauritius, Singapore, and Cyprus to restore source-based capital gains taxation. Governed under Section 90 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, DTAAs prevent tax evasion and dual taxation on international income. Amendments align bilateral treaties with the OECD/G20 Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) framework by introducing the Principal Purpose Test (PPT). Managed by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Ministry of Finance, these tax reforms curb round-tripping, shell company misuse, and aggressive tax avoidance strategies.

articles.title: New Zealand parliament passes India trade deal, cutting tariffs on most exports - Reuters
articles.description: The Parliament of New Zealand has ratified a landmark bilateral trade agreement with India, aimed at drastically reducing tariffs across major export categories. Overseen by India’s Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the pact enhances market access for Indian agricultural goods, textiles, and pharmaceuticals while lowering duty barriers on New Zealand’s dairy alternatives, timber, and kiwi exports. The deal aligns with India’s broader foreign trade strategy to secure Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreements (CEPAs) and Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) with Indo-Pacific economies, strengthening supply chain resilience and expanding bilateral trade volume.

articles.title: Semicon India 2026: Amid ‘weaponisation’ of supply chains, PM pitches India as a ‘trustworthy’ chipmaking destination
articles.description: At Semicon India 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted India as a trustworthy chipmaking destination, emphasizing the need to mitigate the weaponisation of global supply chains. The initiative aligns with the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM), launched by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) with a ₹76,000 crore outlay. ISM aims to position India as a global hub for semiconductor design, manufacturing, and technology development, supporting financial incentives for semiconductor fabs, display fabs, and OSAT facilities under the Digital India program.

articles.title: MEA notifies new rules: 36-page passports for children below 15 to be valid for five years - Moneycontrol.com
articles.description: The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) has notified amendments to the Passport Rules framed under the Passports Act, 1967. Under the updated regulations, 36-page passports issued to children below 15 years of age will now be valid for five years or until the child reaches 18 years of age, whichever is earlier. This regulatory change aims to streamline passport services for minors, ensuring compliance with international civil aviation standards and security norms governing travel documents issued by the Central Government.

articles.title: What lies beyond India’s E20 push
articles.description: India’s push for 20% ethanol-blended petrol (E20) under the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme, spearheaded by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, faces evaluation regarding overall economic efficiency. While aimed at reducing crude oil import dependency and lowering carbon emissions, reports indicate that E20's lower energy density reduces vehicle fuel economy, leading to higher consumer expenditure. The strategy also raises concerns over food security and water intensity due to the diversion of agricultural feedstocks like sugarcane and maize for bio-ethanol production.

articles.title: Supreme Court urges government to make three-language policy mandatory for Class 6 only from January 1, 2027 - The Hindu
articles.description: The Supreme Court urged the Ministry of Education and CBSE to defer the mandatory implementation of the Three-Language Formula for Class 6 students to January 1, 2027. Originally recommended by the Kothari Commission (1968) and reaffirmed in the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the policy mandates teaching three languages, including at least two native Indian languages. The apex court highlighted the need for adequate transition time for students and schools to adapt to curriculum adjustments without impacting academic welfare.

articles.title: ED widens scrutiny of possible irregularities in IBC proceedings | Explained
articles.description: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has expanded its investigation into potential financial irregularities, undervaluation of assets, and money laundering within Corporate Insolvency Resolution Processes under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016. Enacted to ensure time-bound asset value maximization, the IBC is regulated by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. The ED, functioning under the Finance Ministry’s Department of Revenue, is scrutinizing potential misuses under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002.

articles.title: Kolkata-based GRSE launches indigenous ocean research vessel 'Sagar Manthan'
articles.description: Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE), Kolkata, launched 'Sagar Manthan', an indigenous Ocean Research Vessel (ORV) valued at ₹840 crore, expected to be operational by early 2028. Built for oceanographic research and deep-sea exploration, the project supports India's Deep Ocean Mission under the Ministry of Earth Sciences. GRSE, a Miniratna Category-I Defence Public Sector Undertaking (DPSU) under the Ministry of Defence, continues to enhance indigenous capability in specialized scientific shipbuilding.

articles.title: MDR apprehension unlikely to spur higher cash usage: RBI Deputy Governor
articles.description: The Reserve Bank of India clarified that introducing a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) will not spur cash usage. Starting October 15, a 0.4% MDR applies to Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 for payments of ₹75,000 or more. MDR is the fee charged to merchants by processing banks for digital transaction processing. Payable solely by merchants—not consumers—the revenue is split among acquiring banks, payment service providers, and NPCI.

articles.title: NMDC targets Net Zero operational emissions by 2047
articles.description: National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC), a Navratna PSU under the Ministry of Steel, announced a roadmap to achieve Net Zero operational emissions by 2047. Structured into three strategic phases—Short-Term (FY 2026–30), Medium-Term (FY 2030–40), and Long-Term (FY 2040–47)—the initiative focuses on renewable energy integration, energy efficiency, and sustainable mining. India's largest iron ore producer aims to align operational targets with the national commitment of Net Zero by 2070.

articles.title: HAL hands over LCA FOC trainers, first HTT-40 ‘Ankur’ to IAF, 4 Dhruv-NG Choppers to Pawan Hans - timesofindia.indiatimes.com
articles.description: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) handed over two Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas Final Operational Clearance twin-seater trainers and three HTT-40 basic trainers ('Ankur') to the Indian Air Force. Additionally, HAL delivered four Dhruv Next Generation (Dhruv-NG) helicopters to Pawan Hans Limited. Attended by the Defence and Civil Aviation Ministers, the handover strengthens the 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat' initiative. The indigenous HTT-40 trainer aircraft enhances preliminary flight training for IAF pilots.

articles.title: As Project Cheetah completes 4 years, big cat population in India rises to 52 - The Hindu
articles.description: Marking four years of Project Cheetah, India’s cheetah population has increased to 52, boosted by cubs born at Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh. Launched to reintroduce the world's fastest land animal—declared extinct in India in 1952—the intercontinental translocation program brought African cheetahs from Namibia and South Africa. Overseen by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) under the Environment Ministry, current efforts prioritize habitat expansion and establishing a self-sustaining metapopulation.

articles.title: How will the U.S.’s Sanctioning Act affect India? | Explained
articles.description: The U.S. proposed the 'Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, 2026', introducing secondary sanctions and severe tariffs on nations importing Russian oil outside G7 price cap mechanisms. For India, the world's third-largest oil importer, this poses significant risks to its energy security, trade balance, and fiscal deficit management, as Russia remains a major crude supplier. Static GK linkage includes U.S. sanctions frameworks like CAATSA (Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act) and foreign policy waiver provisions managed by the U.S. Department of State.

articles.title: Biometric Aadhaar Authentication Mandatory for Subsidised Domestic LPG Refills from 1 October 2026 - pib.gov.in
articles.description: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has mandated biometric Aadhaar eKYC authentication for domestic consumers to receive subsidised LPG refills starting October 1, 2026. This directive applies to beneficiaries under the PAHAL (Direct Benefit Transfer for LPG) and Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) schemes. Aimed at eliminating ghost beneficiaries, commercial diversion, and subsidy leakage, the initiative leverages UIDAI's Aadhaar ecosystem. Unauthenticated accounts will lose subsidy benefits, strengthening targeted welfare delivery under Section 7 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016.

articles.title: Centre Notifies Appointment Of Judges, Additional Judges At Four High Courts - Live Law
articles.description: The Ministry of Law and Justice notified the appointment of 14 judicial officers as Judges and Additional Judges across four High Courts, including Delhi, following recommendations by the Supreme Court Collegium. The appointments include five women judges, boosting gender representation in the higher judiciary. Statistically, High Court Judges are appointed by the President under Article 217 (Permanent Judges) and Article 224 (Additional Judges) of the Indian Constitution. The process emphasizes judicial vacancies management, collegium system precedents (Third Judges Case), and constitutional governance.

articles.title: India forces caller-ID apps to feed spam reports to telcos - TechCrunch
articles.description: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) issued strict anti-spam guidelines requiring third-party caller-ID applications to share spam reports directly with Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). Under Telecom Unsolicited Commercial Communications (UCC) framework, TRAI mandates explicit customer consent mechanisms, AI-driven spam detection systems, and strict penalties for non-compliant telemarketers. Statutory context links to the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997, and the Telecommunications Act, 2023, enhancing consumer protection, cybersecurity, and regulatory enforcement against financial fraud and unsolicited cold calls.

articles.title: What does the latest revision to the EPFO wage ceiling entail? | Explained
articles.description: The Union Labour Ministry's proposed revision of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) wage ceiling expands mandatory social security coverage under the EPF and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952. Increasing the monthly wage cap enhances pension (EPS) and provident fund (EPF) benefits for formal sector workers, broadening India's social safety net. Key exam aspects include balancing employee take-home pay with employer contribution burdens, statutory governance of EPFO under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, and alignment with the Code on Social Security, 2020.

articles.title: Missing measure in India’s magnet mission
articles.description: India’s critical mineral strategy faces a structural gap in the rare-earth value chain, specifically in converting raw ores into high-performance permanent magnets used in EVs and defence. While India holds significant rare-earth reserves managed by IREL (India Rare Earths Limited) under the Department of Atomic Energy, processing and refining technologies remain heavily monopolized by China. To bolster energy security and reduce import dependence, the Ministry of Mines is emphasizing midstream processing capabilities, midstream separation, and indigenous manufacturing under critical mineral initiatives.

articles.title: ASML begins India operations, links scaling-up plan with success of Tata Electronics, govt ambition - Moneycontrol.com
articles.description: Dutch semiconductor equipment giant ASML has initiated operations in India, anchoring its expansion to the success of domestic semiconductor initiatives like Tata Electronics' fab plant in Dholera, Gujarat. ASML dominates global photolithography systems essential for manufacturing microchips. This development aligns with the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), which aims to establish a robust domestic chip manufacturing ecosystem, reduce import dependence, and integrate India into the global technology supply chain.

articles.title: Old era of jingoism, equating Nepali nationalism with anti-Indianism, is over: Nepal Finance Minister - The Hindu
articles.description: Nepal’s Finance Minister emphasized resetting bilateral ties with India, signaling a shift away from anti-India rhetoric toward economic pragmatic partnership. India-Nepal relations are guided by the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship and India's 'Neighbourhood First' policy. Key areas of cooperation include cross-border trade, power export agreements, and connectivity projects like Integrated Check Posts (ICPs) and railway links. Strengthening economic integration with Nepal is strategic for India's regional stability and countering growing external influence in South Asia.

articles.title: India's exports to core BRICS markets surge 34% in April-August; China leads
articles.description: India’s exports to core BRICS nations grew by 34% during April–August of the current fiscal year, raising the bloc's share in India's total outbound trade from 8.1% to 9.2%. China emerged as the leading driver of this growth. The BRICS grouping, which expanded recently to include new members, serves as a vital economic platform for Global South cooperation. According to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, market diversification within BRICS strengthens India's trade resilience amidst global macroeconomic headwinds.

articles.title: India, Japan Air Force Chiefs fly the Tejas during Exercise 'Veer Guardian-2026' in Jodhpur - ANI News
articles.description: The Indian Air Force (IAF) and Japan Air Self-Defense Force (JASDF) conducted the bilateral air exercise 'Veer Guardian-2026' in Jodhpur, featuring IAF's indigenous LCA Tejas, Su-30MKI, Rafale, and Japanese F-2A fighters. Demonstrating strategic synergy, both Air Chiefs flew the Tejas fighter jet. Exercise Veer Guardian reinforces defence cooperation between Quad partners in the Indo-Pacific region. Strategic exercises with Japan also include Dharma Guardian (Army) and JIMEX (Navy), underscoring deepening bilateral security ties.

articles.title: New checklist by Keralam research team records 3,261 flowering plant species in Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve
articles.description: Researchers from the Jawaharlal Nehru Tropical Botanic Garden and Research Institute (JNTBGRI), Kerala, compiled a comprehensive checklist recording 3,261 flowering plant species in the Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve. Spanning the southern Western Ghats across Kerala and Tamil Nadu, Agasthyamalai was designated a UNESCO World Biosphere Reserve in 2016. Highlighting the Western Ghats' status as a global biodiversity hotspot, the study emphasizes targeted, region-specific conservation strategies, endemic species preservation, and botanical documentation essential for forest management and competitive exam static GK on protected areas.

articles.title: India-New Zealand FTA ratified, to come into effect on October 20
articles.description: India and New Zealand have ratified a landmark Free Trade Agreement (FTA), set to take effect on October 20. Under the agreement, New Zealand will eliminate tariffs on 100% of Indian imports, while India will eliminate or reduce tariffs on 95% of imports from New Zealand. Aimed at doubling bilateral trade, the pact safeguards India's sensitive sectors, including dairy and key agricultural commodities, from import surges. This trade initiative falls under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry's push for global market expansion and trade diversification.

articles.title: Whole of govt. approach being followed to address concerns of critical mineral recycling industry: G. Kishan Reddy
articles.description: Union Minister of Mines G. Kishan Reddy announced a comprehensive Whole-of-Government approach to support India's critical mineral recycling industry. Critical minerals such as lithium, cobalt, nickel, and rare earth elements are vital for high-tech manufacturing, clean energy transitions, and electric vehicles. By streamlining regulatory frameworks and supporting domestic recycling technology, the Ministry aims to secure sustainable supply chains, reduce import dependence, promote a circular economy, and align with India’s broader strategic climate goals under the National Critical Minerals initiative.

articles.title: EAM S. Jaishankar to lead Indian delegation at 81st Session of UNGA in New York - News On AIR
articles.description: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar is leading the Indian delegation at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) session in New York. Prior to his address, the EAM reviewed bilateral momentum, including economic ties with EFTA member states like Switzerland and Liechtenstein. Key discussions at multilateral forums center on global governance reform, South-South cooperation, supply chain resilience, and trade issues. For competitive exams, the event highlights India’s active multilateral diplomacy, international relations under the Ministry of External Affairs, and ongoing strategic dialogues with European partners.

articles.title: ASML enters India: What does its Tata partnership mean for country’s semiconductor ambitions? - Livemint
articles.description: Dutch semiconductor equipment major ASML has partnered with Tata Group to strengthen India’s emerging semiconductor ecosystem. ASML is the global leader in advanced photolithography systems essential for microchip manufacturing. This strategic collaboration aligns with the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) spearheaded by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). The partnership boosts domestic chip fabrication, chip assembly, testing, and packaging (ATMP) capabilities, reducing foreign dependency and positioning India as a resilient hub in global technology supply chains under the ISM incentive framework.

articles.title: World Rhino Day focus on India-Bhutan joint conservation
articles.description: A translocation programme helped the one-horned rhino population in Manas Tiger Reserve from zero to 48 in 20 years, but increasing movement of the herbivore across the international border has raised new concerns
